accuracy.evidence: Matched to the DfE Year 3 measurement statement 'measure, compare, add and subtract: lengths (m/cm/mm); mass (kg/g); volume/capacity (l/ml)' and to the topic's evidence lines (measure in cm and mm, weigh in g and kg, add two measures in the same unit). Every number checked by hand: 74, 52 and 38 mm readings; 45 + 38 = 83 (73 is the lost exchange); 1 m 30 cm = 130 cm, 130 + 85 = 215 cm = 2 m 15 cm (116 is 1 + 30 + 85); 350 + 400 = 750 g, halfway between the 700 and 800 marks on a dial with 50 g divisions; 1000 − 250 − 250 = 500 ml; 41 − 23 = 18 by hops 7 + 10 + 1. Unit facts 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 l = 1000 ml are SI definitions. Challenge answers 140, 83, 700, 36, 450 g, 600, 17 cm rechecked.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common Year 3 measure slips listed in the adult text: adding mixed units as if equal (1 m + 40 cm = 41, rope prediction 116 cm, tag unit), 1 kg = 100 g or 1 l treated as 1 (998 ml after pouring, tag kg), reading every scale division as 1 (705 g, tag scale), cm/mm confusion (7 mm or 520 mm for a 52 mm crayon, tag mm), losing the exchanged ten (73 cm, tag carry), and adding when the question asks for a difference (64 cm growth, tag add).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmcalc is built on calculating with measures: a mm ruler that accepts a tap only at the true end, a ribbon that must be dragged to meet another end to end before a total is accepted, a conversion card that must be tapped before mixed units can be added, a 50 g-division dial whose needle moves as bags are added, a 1 litre jug that drains 250 ml per glass, and a number line whose hops build a difference. flagcmpm compares with < > =, flagunits picks units, flaglenht/flagmass/flagcups use non-standard units; the shingle gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The canvas shows the result before the rule: the joined ribbon visibly ends at 83 on the metre stick, the converted label changes to 130 cm before the add is allowed, the needle settles at 750 g where 350 + 400 also lands, the jug level drops to the 500 ml mark, and the hops 7, 10 and 1 sit on the line before 18 is chosen. Step text then confirms the unit rule or method.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 7 mm for a 7 cm 4 mm pencil, 73 cm for 45 + 38, 'Nothing, it is right' for Jo's 116 cm, 705 g for a needle halfway between 700 and 800, and 'Add: 23 + 41' for how much a plant grew. Each is disproved by the canvas in the same step.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge items, each with two tagged wrong answers (unit, carry, kg, mm, scale, add, sub); every message names the slip, e.g. 'The units are different. 1 m is 100 cm, so change it before you add.' and 'Work out what each small mark is worth before you read the scale.' Wrong lab taps also name the slip ('73 forgets the ten made by 5 + 8 = 13.', '998: you took away 2, not 2 glasses of 250 ml').

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and Year 3 terms used precisely (millimetre, centimetre, metre, gram, kilogram, litre, millilitre, end to end, difference); the adult text passes the family readability limit in validate_lessons on the first run.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean. Each kid paragraph carries one rule (mm on a ruler, adding lengths with an exchange, convert before adding, g and ml use 1000) and each lab step practises one calculation type from the Year 3 statement.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots after Show me on every step; messages wrap instead of shrinking; the 23/41 labels on the growth line collided with 25/40 on the first shot and were moved below the line; ruler numbers drop to every 20 cm on narrow screens. Young mode gives 56 px buttons; drag on the ribbon and taps on ruler, bags and glasses were tested on iPhone 13 with no page errors.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (three mm readings, Join end to end, 1 m = 100 cm, Add flour / sugar, Pour 250 ml, Next hop, and answer buttons); the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every reading, result and challenge question; walk.cjs reports axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 3 Measurement (measure, compare, add and subtract lengths m/cm/mm, mass kg/g, volume/capacity l/ml) and Year 2 Measurement (choose and use standard units; compare and order with >, < and =)
BIPM, The International System of Units (SI brochure): prefixes milli (10^-3), centi (10^-2) and kilo (10^3), giving 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 l = 1000 ml
